+title: Create the nested IntegrationTests package with a loud availability precondition
+---
+## What
+
+Recreate `IntegrationTests/` as a nested SwiftPM package holding the real-model suite. It drives Apple Intelligence through `LanguageModelSession(model: .default)` and needs **no new dependencies** — `FoundationModels` is an OS framework and FoundationModelsRanker already ships `extension LanguageModelSession: AgentSession`.
+
+This card builds only the skeleton and the shared support. The two tests come next, in `^<test1>` and `^<test3>`.
+
+Files to create:
+- `IntegrationTests/Package.swift` — `name: "FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryIntegrationTests"`, `platforms: [.macOS("27.0")]`, one dependency `.package(path: "..")`, one test target depending on `.product(name: "FoundationModelsMetadataRegistry", package: "FoundationModelsMetadataRegistry")`. Model the shape on the deleted manifest at `git show cafac33^:IntegrationTests/Package.swift`, minus every Router/MLX/Hugging Face entry.
+- `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryIntegrationTests/Support/ModelAvailability.swift` — the loud precondition, below.
+- `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryIntegrationTests/Support/IntegrationCatalog.swift` — the shared fixture catalog, below.
+
+### The root package exports only one product
+
+`Package.swift:137-142` declares exactly one library, `FoundationModelsMetadataRegistry`. A package can import only its dependencies' *products*, so this suite **cannot** reach `ExamplesSupport`, `CatalogSearchCore`, or any `Examples/` type. It must define its own fixtures. Do not add a product to the root package to work around this.
+
+### Fail loudly, do not skip
+
+The user chose loud failure over skipping. The org's CI runners are self-hosted macOS 27 machines with Apple Intelligence enabled — proven by FoundationModelsRanker's CI run 33318330212, whose integration job ran 4 real-model tests successfully — so an unavailable model is a real problem, not an expected environment.
+
+Read `SystemLanguageModel.default.availability`. It is a synchronous, non-throwing property. `Availability` is `@frozen` with `available` and `unavailable(UnavailableReason)`. `UnavailableReason` is **not** frozen and has `deviceNotEligible`, `appleIntelligenceNotEnabled`, `modelNotReady` — so a `switch` over it needs `@unknown default`.
+
+Write `ModelAvailability.requireAvailable()` that records a test failure naming the exact reason when the model is not available. Every test calls it first. Do not use `.enabled(if:)`, which would silently pass.
+
+### The fixture catalog
+
+A small `SearchableMetadata` conformer with stable ids and short blocks — a handful of git subcommands is proven material for this package. Keep the assembled prefix comfortably under `SelectionConfig.defaultCapacityCharacterLimit` (32,000) so both tests stay on the under-budget cached-root path; the over-budget path is deliberately out of scope.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `swift build --package-path IntegrationTests` succeeds.
+- [ ] `IntegrationTests/Package.swift` declares exactly one dependency, `.package(path: "..")`.
+- [ ] The suite compiles with no reference to Router, MLX, Hugging Face, or any `Examples/` type.
+- [ ] `ModelAvailability.requireAvailable()` fails the test, naming the `UnavailableReason`, when the model is unavailable.
+- [ ] The root `swift test` still runs 114 tests and does not reach this package.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] Add one placeholder test in the nested suite that calls `ModelAvailability.requireAvailable()` and asserts `SystemLanguageModel.default.isAvailable`. Run `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests` — it passes on this machine, where availability was measured as `available`.
+- [ ] Temporarily invert the precondition to prove it can fail, confirm the failure message names a reason, then revert.
+- [ ] Run `swift test` at the root. 114 tests pass, unchanged.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
